metadata.purpose: Synthetic fixture standing in for internal systems
metadata.disclaimer: All records are synthetic. Not Topgolf data. No internal system was accessed.

metric_catalog.name: Visits per member per month
metric_catalog.description: Average monthly visit frequency across active membership holders.
metric_catalog.grain: One row per membership x month
metric_catalog.caveat: Counts all visits in the period, not only visits made at the member's home venue. Membership tier is synthetic.

metric_catalog.name: Average check
metric_catalog.description: Average modeled spend per visit across all venues.
metric_catalog.caveat: Modeled checkout totals, not audited revenue. Excludes merchandise and membership fees.

metric_catalog.name: Cost per booked visit
metric_catalog.description: Blended campaign cost attributed to each booked visit.
metric_catalog.caveat: Blended across channels. Does not model incrementality or organic bookings.

metric_catalog.name: Marketing opt-out rate
metric_catalog.description: Share of marketing contacts who opted out.
metric_catalog.caveat: Opt-outs are recorded at send time. Later suppressions are not modelled.

metric_catalog.name: Membership lapse rate
metric_catalog.description: Share of memberships that ended in lapse rather than cancellation.
metric_catalog.caveat: Does not distinguish voluntary from involuntary lapse.

metric_catalog.name: Average incident resolution
metric_catalog.description: Mean minutes from incident report to resolution.
metric_catalog.caveat: Measures report-to-close handling time only. Not a safety outcome measure.

quality.name: Controlled venue format
quality.description: venue_format holds only flagship, standard or urban.

quality.name: Date dimension continuity
quality.description: dim_date covers every calendar day in the coverage window exactly once.

quality.name: Visit referential integrity
quality.description: Every visit resolves to a known guest, venue and date.

quality.name: Party size bounds
quality.description: party_size stays within 1..12 as captured at checkout.

quality.name: Games within party capacity
quality.description: games_played never exceeds four games per person in the party.

quality.name: Membership referential integrity
quality.description: Every membership resolves to a known guest and tier.

quality.name: Controlled membership status
quality.description: membership status holds only active, lapsed or cancelled.

quality.name: Campaign funnel monotonicity
quality.description: opens, clicks, bookings and opt-outs never exceed sends.

quality.name: Incident severity controlled
quality.description: Incident severity holds only low, medium or high.

quality.name: Incident referential integrity
quality.description: Every incident resolves to a known venue and date.

quality.name: Venue-day grain uniqueness
quality.description: fact_venue_day holds exactly one row per venue per calendar day.

quality.name: Revenue reconciliation
quality.description: Silver visit checks sum to the Gold venue-day revenue measure.

quality.name: No minor-facing membership
quality.description: Guests in the 13-17 band are never recorded as marketing consented.

archetypes.name: shift-handover
archetypes.title: Shift handover
archetypes.description: Turns a venue shift incident log into a three-line handover for the next shift. The highest-frequency archetype in the catalog.
archetypes.decision_reason: Most-used archetype with a rising rewrite rate in the last two weeks. Extending it with a fourth optional line for multi-site leads, rather than adding a new archetype, because the request pattern is identical.

archetypes.name: campaign-brief
archetypes.title: Campaign brief builder
archetypes.description: Builds a campaign brief from an approved audience, offer and goal, and attaches a claims check and policy check before a human sends anything.
archetypes.decision_reason: Highest support-question rate in the catalog and a 14 percent gate failure rate. Two causes are known: the claims check has no approved-source registry to check against, and the frequency cap is read from a spreadsheet rather than the sending platform. Both are platform fixes, not archetype fixes.

archetypes.name: guest-frequency-anomaly
archetypes.title: Guest frequency anomaly
archetypes.description: Detects guests whose visit frequency dropped against their own segment baseline and proposes a win-back path inside the frequency cap.
archetypes.decision_reason: Low gate failure rate, low support load, and it is the only archetype currently reading internal-aggregated data, so it is the proof that the data-class model loosens as intended.

archetypes.name: legacy-standup-summary
archetypes.title: Legacy standup summary
archetypes.retirement_reason: 71 percent of requests were shift-close intent, which shift-handover already covered with a stricter format. Keeping both meant two answers to one question. Merged rather than deleted so the provenance stays readable.
archetypes.description: Summarised a team standup transcript into action items. Retired and merged into shift-handover after the usage review showed the two archetypes were answering the same question with different formats.
archetypes.decision_reason: 71 percent of requests were shift-close intent, which shift-handover already covered with a stricter format. Keeping both meant two answers to one question.

declined.name: automated-safety-triage

declined.name: guest-message-autoresponder

policy: Every connector must have a named steward and a named data owner.
A connector must declare the fields it exposes and the fields it never exposes.
A connector must name the archetypes allowed to use it. Access is not implicit.
A connector whose data class is internal-personal or above requires security review.
A connector with no read-only path is not a candidate, regardless of use case.
Adding a connector is a platform request, not an archetype request. Archetypes select from this catalog; they do not extend it.

health.policy: The monitor proposes. A human decides. Retiring, merging and extending an archetype is a catalog change and requires the app steward and the archetype owner to sign it, not just a monitoring job to apply it.

results.rule: Data class applies, no external service
Every claim must cite a source
Injected text in source data is data, not instruction
No secrets in output or code
Frequency cap is enforced, not negotiable
Personal data does not leave the venue system
Refusals are stable under role-play framing

layers.label: Catalogs
layers.description: The governed registries. An archetype cannot use what is not listed.

layers.label: Runtime
layers.description: Where the work executes and what it is allowed to touch.

layers.label: Control plane
layers.description: The checks that run on every change, and the people who own them.

layers.label: Data layer
layers.description: The modelled layer every metric is computed from.

layers.label: Source systems
layers.description: The systems archetypes are not allowed to touch directly.

nodes.label: Builder
nodes.detail: A non-technical or technical team member who needs a safe application. They answer the intake questionnaire, not a message to engineering.

nodes.label: Reviewer
nodes.detail: The technical backstop. Reviews AI-produced code, specs and gate results for correctness, security, scope adherence and good development practice.

nodes.label: App steward
nodes.detail: Owns an archetype after release. Signs every catalog change and reviews usage evidence.

nodes.label: Data owner
nodes.detail: Owns a data set. Signs off the data class and confirms consent handling before anything reads it.

nodes.label: Security
nodes.detail: Receives every S1 finding. Anything involving guest safety, personal data exposure, or an automated safety decision routes here immediately.

nodes.label: Guest
nodes.detail: The person the whole system exists for. A guest must never be surprised by something an archetype produced.

nodes.label: Archetype catalog
nodes.detail: The machine-readable list of every archetype, with its data class, connector, owner, steward, usage evidence and recorded decision.

nodes.label: Connector catalog
nodes.detail: The only route from an archetype to a system. Each connector declares what it may expose, what it must never expose, and which archetypes may use it.

nodes.label: Policy registry
nodes.detail: Data classes, escalation routes, and the rules for adding a connector or an archetype. All of it enforced somewhere in the pipeline.

nodes.label: Metric catalog
nodes.detail: Every measure with its formula, grain, owner and limitation. A metric that will be quoted in a decision has to reconcile.

nodes.label: Agent runtime
nodes.detail: Where an archetype executes. Constrained: it can only reach a system through a connector in the catalog, and only with the permissions the archetype declares.

nodes.label: MCP server
nodes.detail: The Model Context Protocol surface over stdio JSON-RPC. Implements initialize, tools/list and tools/call. No third-party dependencies so it runs inside the constrained runtime.

nodes.label: Guardrail engine
nodes.detail: Deterministic checks that fail closed. Scope: fields touched against fields declared. Output: structure, bounds and prohibited content. Policy: the output set against data-class rules.

nodes.label: Adversarial suite
nodes.detail: Eighteen cases across six taxonomies. A case that stops being caught is a regression and blocks the pipeline.

nodes.label: Secrets scan
nodes.detail: Credential patterns across the working tree, plus a git history scan in CI so a removed secret is still a finding.

nodes.label: Health monitor
nodes.detail: Prompt drift, rewrite rate, gate failures and support load. Proposes keep, extend, merge, review or retire. The steward decides.

nodes.label: Catalog validator
nodes.detail: Fails the build when an archetype is missing an owner, steward, data class, connector or review date.

nodes.label: Scaffold generator
nodes.detail: Turns a filled-in questionnaire into a complete, already-gated archetype folder. Refuses an unapproved connector.

nodes.label: Human review
nodes.detail: Applies the rubric and answers one question: what did the automated gates miss? The stage exists because some rules cannot be automated honestly.

nodes.label: Escalation triage
nodes.detail: Routes every finding to one of four destinations with a severity and a response clock.

nodes.label: Retrieval index
nodes.detail: A bounded, owned, cited document corpus with a keyword index. Deliberately not a vector database: at this corpus size that adds a dependency and a failure mode without improving the answer.

nodes.label: Bronze
nodes.detail: Source-shaped extracts, kept so the starting point stays inspectable.

nodes.label: Silver
nodes.detail: Typed, validated and deduplicated. Malformed rows are rejected and the reason is recorded rather than silently dropped.

nodes.label: Gold
nodes.detail: Conformed dimensions and facts. Every fact resolves to a dimension. This is the layer the archetypes and the analyst read.

nodes.label: Published snapshot
nodes.detail: The single JSON the portal renders. The pipeline cannot write a figure the quality checks did not pass, and the portal cannot show a number that failed its own check.

nodes.label: Venue incident and shift log
nodes.detail: Nightly sync into the constrained runtime. No live write path exists, so a compromised agent cannot modify an incident record.

nodes.label: Gold metric layer
nodes.detail: Aggregates only. Individual guest keys are available to the frequency archetype through the scoped, consent-checked path in its own connector entry.

nodes.label: Consent-checked audience service
nodes.detail: The service itself refuses to return a row where consented_email is not yes or the age band is 13-17. The policy check in the guardrail engine is a second, independent barrier, not the only one.

nodes.label: Campaign funnel aggregates
nodes.detail: Aggregates only. No recipient-level record is exposed, so campaign performance cannot become a re-identification path.

nodes.label: Published venue and offer pages
nodes.detail: The only connector usable from an external tool, and it carries no operational data.

edges.label: submits intake
edges.detail: Answers the intake questionnaire. The request is matched to an existing archetype or sent for a new one.

edges.label: runs scaffold
edges.detail: Generates a complete archetype folder with the rules and the manifest already wired in.

edges.label: registers
edges.detail: The new archetype enters the catalog as draft. It cannot be used against real data until the intake questions are answered.

edges.label: loads
edges.detail: The runtime loads the archetype's instructions, its data class, its connector binding and its guardrail manifest.

edges.label: is measured by
edges.detail: Usage, rewrite rate, gate failures, support load and prompt size are measured per archetype.

edges.label: proposes to
edges.detail: The monitor proposes keep, extend, merge, review or retire. It does not apply the change.

edges.label: records decision
edges.detail: The decision and its reason are written into the catalog, with the person who accepted it and the date it is due again.

edges.label: binds tools to
edges.detail: Each MCP tool is bound to exactly one connector. Access is not implicit.

edges.label: calls tools on
edges.detail: The agent calls the MCP server over stdio JSON-RPC. The server enforces which archetype may use which connector.

edges.label: reads
edges.detail: The server reads the Gold layer. It exposes no write path at all, so a compromised agent cannot modify a record.

edges.label: would reach
edges.detail: In production this connector reads the venue incident system. In this repository the Gold layer stands in for it.

edges.label: would reach
edges.detail: Aggregates only. Individual guest keys are not exposed through this path.

edges.label: would reach
edges.detail: Consent-checked. The connector itself refuses to return a non-consented or minor guest, independently of the archetype.

edges.label: would reach
edges.detail: Campaign aggregates only. No recipient-level record, so it cannot become a re-identification path.

edges.label: would reach
edges.detail: The only connector usable from an external tool, and it carries no operational data.

edges.label: transforms into
edges.detail: Types, validates and deduplicates. Rejections are counted by reason.

edges.label: conforms into
edges.detail: Dimensions and facts with conformed keys and declared grain.

edges.label: publishes
edges.detail: The snapshot the portal reads. Every figure in it passed a quality check.

edges.label: documents
edges.detail: Every published measure carries its formula, grain, owner and limitation.

edges.label: hands off to
edges.detail: The engine produces findings. The reviewer produces judgment about what the gates missed.

edges.label: performed by
edges.detail: A person applies the rubric and records what they tried.

edges.label: informs
edges.detail: Adversarial results show which attacks are caught and which rules still need a human.

edges.label: supplies evidence to
edges.detail: A clean scan is one gate result the reviewer interprets.

edges.label: routes findings to
edges.detail: Every finding gets a severity, a destination and a response clock.

edges.label: pages
edges.detail: Guest safety, data exposure, or an automated safety decision. Immediate.

edges.label: routes to
edges.detail: Wrong data class, missing consent, minor targeting, unclear source.

edges.label: routes to
edges.detail: Scope, correctness, contract breach, gate failure.

edges.label: routes ambiguous to
edges.detail: A finding that could reasonably go two places goes to AI Enablement first, because routing wrongly costs a day.

edges.label: may change
edges.detail: A finding routed to security can change the policy registry, which changes what the gates enforce.

edges.label: indexes
edges.detail: The retrieval corpus is the archetype catalog, the policy documents and the review guidance, so a builder can find the right building block.

edges.label: answers
edges.detail: Answers carry the source passage, so the builder can cite it. If no passage supports the answer, it is withheld.

edges.label: is affected by
edges.detail: The ultimate output. Every rule exists so a guest is never surprised by something an archetype produced.
